description: Find the moon phase for any date: phase name, illumination percentage, moon age and the next full and new moons — computed with the standard synodic-month algorithm.

faqs.a: From the moon's age in the 29.530588853-day synodic cycle, measured from the known new moon of 6 January 2000, 18:14 UTC. Illumination follows from (1 − cos(2π·age/cycle)) / 2.
Approximate: typically within about a day of the true phase. It is a simplified astronomical algorithm, not a full ephemeris.
New Moon, Waxing Crescent, First Quarter, Waxing Gibbous, Full Moon, Waning Gibbous, Last Quarter and Waning Crescent.

howto: Read the phase name, emoji, illumination and moon age instantly.
See the dates of the next new moon and next full moon.
Remember the result is approximate — good to about a day.
